findings.title: Small-action button no longer stays on the right edge
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex row (flexbox() and align-items(center) at the top of the rule), but its delete/recover button is still only positioned with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, so a direct-child button (the usual Discourse small-action markup: avatar, description, then the times button) stays in source order instead of pinning to the row's right edge. Even if the button is nested in .small-action-desc, that description is a default flex item (flex: 0 1 auto, no flex-grow) and now has only padding: 0 1.5% instead of a full-width block with 4em left padding, so a float inside it aligns to the text, not the far side of the post. The X that used to sit at the right of closed/pinned/similar action rows now sits immediately beside the action text and is easy to mis-click next to the username. Browsers that ignore flexbox still honor .topic-avatar { float: left }, and the 4em padding that kept the description clear of that 45px icon is gone, so the text runs through the icon. Give the description flex: 1 and min-width: 0, put margin-left: auto and flex-shrink: 0 on the button, and stop using float for either child.

findings.title: order mixin writes 0-based values into 1-based box-ordinal-group
findings.body: @mixin order($val) copies $val unchanged onto -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group as well as the modern order property. The 2009 box-ordinal-group property is 1-based and defaults to 1; modern order is 0-based and defaults to 0. Those prefixed declarations therefore do not implement order (the usual fix, used by Autoprefixer, is $val + 1). order(0) emits an invalid box-ordinal-group: 0, and order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of coming after them. The new call sites pass 2 and 3 (.d-header .panel and .extra-info-wrapper), which still sort after the default group, so those two values happen to keep the same sequence in old WebKit/Firefox — but the shared mixin is wrong for every other value and should not be merged as the compatibility layer.

findings.title: Header panel right-alignment has no working legacy fallback
findings.body: .d-header .panel was float: right and .d-header .title was float: left. Both floats were removed and the panel is now only pushed right with margin-left: auto, while .contents is a flex container via the new flexbox() mixin. Auto main-axis margins absorb free space only in the 2012+ flex model (display: flex / -webkit-flex / -ms-flexbox). flexbox() also emits display: -webkit-box. Browsers that honor that 2009 value and not the later display values (stock Android 4.1–4.3, older iOS) lay the header out as an old horizontal box: floats on the flex items are ignored and margin-left: auto does not push, so the logo and the icon/login cluster sit together on the left. Browsers with no flexbox at all ignore every display value in the mixin; margin-left: auto on a block with width: auto computes to 0, so title and panel stack as full-width blocks. Theme CSS that still right-aligns .panel with float stops working for the same reason. Do not emit 2009 display values unless a 2009 spacer (-webkit-box-flex) actually pins the panel, and keep the float rules as the non-flex fallback.
